label: midbrain-hindbrain boundary maturation during neural plate development
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines midbrain-hindbrain boundary maturation during neural plate development as: A developmental process occurring before the brain has been specified along the neural axis that is required for the midbrain-hindbrain boundary to attain its fully functional state. The midbrain-hindbrain domain of the embryonic brain is comprised of the mesencephalic vesicle and the first rhombencephalic vesicle at early somitogenesis stages. An organizing center at the boundary patterns the midbrain and hindbrain primordia of the neural plate.

label: organism emergence from protective structure
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines organism emergence from protective structure as: The developmental process in which an organism emerges from a surrounding protective structure such as an egg or pupa case.

label: transcytosis
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines transcytosis as: The directed movement of endocytosed material through the cell and its exocytosis from the plasma membrane at the opposite side.

label: pattern specification process
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines pattern specification process as: Any developmental process that results in the creation of defined areas or spaces within an organism to which cells respond and eventually are instructed to differentiate.

label: pupation
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines pupation as: The act of becoming a pupa, a resting stage in the life cycle of organisms with complete metamorphosis. This event marks the end of the prepupal period and the beginning of the pupal period.

label: molting cycle
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines molting cycle as: The periodic casting off and regeneration of an outer covering of cuticle, feathers, hair, horns, skin, etc.

label: molting cycle process
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines molting cycle process as: A multicellular organismal process involved in the periodic casting off and regeneration of an outer covering of cuticle, feathers, hair, horns, skin.

label: scab formation
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines scab formation as: Formation of hardened covering (a scab) at a wound site. The scab has multiple functions including limiting blood loss, providing structural stability to the wound and guarding against infection.

label: organ growth
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines organ growth as: The increase in size or mass of an organ. Organs are commonly observed as visibly distinct structures, but may also exist as loosely associated clusters of cells that function together as to perform a specific function.

label: seed germination
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines seed germination as: The physiological and developmental changes that occur in a seed commencing with water uptake (imbibition) and terminating with the elongation of the embryonic axis.

label: plasma lipoprotein particle clearance
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines plasma lipoprotein particle clearance as: The process in which a lipoprotein particle is removed from the blood via receptor-mediated endocytosis and its constituent parts degraded.

label: cytokine production
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines cytokine production as: The appearance of a cytokine due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.

label: biological process involved in symbiotic interaction
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines biological process involved in symbiotic interaction as: A process carried out by gene products in an organism that enable the organism to engage in a symbiotic relationship, a more or less intimate association, with another organism. The various forms of symbiosis include parasitism, in which the association is disadvantageous or destructive to one of the organisms; mutualism, in which the association is advantageous, or often necessary to one or both and not harmful to either; and commensalism, in which one member of the association benefits while the other is not affected. However, mutualism, parasitism, and commensalism are often not discrete categories of interactions and should rather be perceived as a continuum of interaction ranging from parasitism to mutualism. In fact, the direction of a symbiotic interaction can change during the lifetime of the symbionts due to developmental changes as well as changes in the biotic/abiotic environment in which the interaction occurs. Microscopic symbionts are often referred to as endosymbionts.

label: hematophagy
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines hematophagy as: A feeding behavior that involves the ingestion of blood. Hematophagous animals have mouth parts and chemical agents for penetrating vascular structures in the skin of hosts. To overcome natural hemostasis, vasoconstriction, inflammation, and pain sensation in the host, hematophagous animals pre-inject chemical substances with anesthetic and/or anticoagulant properties.

label: formation of structure involved in a symbiotic process
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines formation of structure involved in a symbiotic process as: The progression of an organism from an initial condition to a later condition, occurring when the organism is in a symbiotic interaction.

label: disruption of anatomical structure in another organism
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines disruption of anatomical structure in another organism as: The disruption of an anatomical structure of another organism, leading to damage or temporary subversion of that structure.

label: modulation of process of another organism
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines modulation of process of another organism as: A process in which an organism effects a change in a biological process in another organism.

label: nitric oxide storage
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines nitric oxide storage as: The accumulation and maintenance in cells or tissues of nitric oxide (NO). Nitric oxide is stored in the form of dinitrosyl-iron complexes, which are stabilized, and possibly sequestered, by binding to glutathione S-transferase proteins.

label: organelle localization
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines organelle localization as: Any process in which an organelle is transported to, and/or maintained in, a specific location.

label: macromolecule localization
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines macromolecule localization as: Any process in which a macromolecule is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location.

label: receptor localization to synapse
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines receptor localization to synapse as: Any process in which a receptor is transported to, and/or maintained at the synapse, the junction between a nerve fiber of one neuron and another neuron or muscle fiber or glial cell.

label: chemical homeostasis
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines chemical homeostasis as: Any biological process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of a chemical.

label: cellular homeostasis
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines cellular homeostasis as: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state at the level of the cell.

label: detoxification of free heme
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines detoxification of free heme as: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of free heme. These include transport of heme away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of heme.

label: toxin catabolic process
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines toxin catabolic process as: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of toxin, a poisonous compound (typically a protein) that is produced by cells or organisms and that can cause disease when introduced into the body or tissues of an organism.

label: mycothiol-dependent detoxification
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines mycothiol-dependent detoxification as: The chemical reactions using mycothiol to convert an alkylating agent to an S-conjugate of mycothiol. The latter is cleaved to release mercapturic acid which is excreted from the cell.

label: detoxification of nitrogen compound
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines detoxification of nitrogen compound as: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of nitrogenous compounds which are dangerous or toxic. This includes the aerobic conversion of toxic compounds to harmless substances.

label: detoxification of inorganic compound
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines detoxification of inorganic compound as: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of inorganic compounds. These include transport of such compounds away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of inorganic compounds.

label: detoxification of endogenously produced metabolite
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines detoxification of endogenously produced metabolite as: A process that reduces or removes the toxicity of an endogenously produced substance. Mechanisms of resistance to endogenously produced compounds include modification the compound, export, sequestration, or mutations in the target enzyme.

label: detoxification of arsenic-containing substance
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines detoxification of arsenic-containing substance as: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of compounds containing arsenic, including arsenates, arsenites, and arsenides. These include transport of such compounds away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of arsenic or arsenic-containing compounds.

label: viral capsid
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines viral capsid as: The protein coat that surrounds the infective nucleic acid in some virus particles. It comprises numerous regularly arranged subunits, or capsomeres.

label: viral capsid, internal space
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines viral capsid, internal space as: The region of a virus contained within the capsid shell, and usually containing the viral genome and accessory proteins.

label: virion nucleoid
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines virion nucleoid as: The region of a virion in which the nucleic acid is confined.

label: virion membrane
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines virion membrane as: The lipid bilayer surrounding a virion.

label: viral nucleocapsid
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines viral nucleocapsid as: The complete protein-nucleic acid complex that is the packaged form of the genome in a virus particle.

label: viral inner capsid
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines viral inner capsid as: The inner layer of a double or triple concentric icosahedral capsid. Inner capsids are part of reoviridae and cystoviridae virions.

label: viral outer capsid
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines viral outer capsid as: The outer layer of a double or triple concentric icosahedral capsid. Outer capsids are part of reoviridae and cystoviridae virions.

label: viral intermediate capsid
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines viral intermediate capsid as: The intermediate layer of a triple concentric icosahedral capsid. Intermediate capsids are part of reoviridae virions.

label: virus tail, shaft
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines virus tail, shaft as: The tube of the non-contractile tails of some viruses.

label: virus tail, sheath
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines virus tail, sheath as: The external contractile envelope of the tail of some viruses. Its contraction ensures ejection of the virus DNA into the host cytoplasm.

label: icosahedral viral capsid, spike
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines icosahedral viral capsid, spike as: A short structure attached to an icosahedral virion capsid, and used for attachment to the host cell.

label: virus tail, fiber
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines virus tail, fiber as: The fibrous region of the virus tail used to scan, recognize and attach to the host cell.

label: viral procapsid
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines viral procapsid as: A stable empty viral capsid produced during the assembly of viruses.

label: virus tail, tip
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines virus tail, tip as: The basal end of the virus tail, which is used by the virus to attach to the host cell.

label: viral tegument
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines viral tegument as: A structure lying between the capsid and envelope of a virus, varying in thickness and often distributed asymmetrically.

label: capsomere
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines capsomere as: Any of the protein subunits that comprise the closed shell or coat (capsid) of certain viruses.

label: virus tail, tube
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines virus tail, tube as: The internal tube of the tail of some viruses. The virus tail tube is the channel for DNA ejection into the host cytoplasm.

label: virus tail
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines virus tail as: Part of the virion that may be used to recognize, attach and inject the viral genome and accessory proteins into the host cell.

label: virus tail, baseplate
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines virus tail, baseplate as: Multiprotein component at the distal (head) end of the virus tail to which fibers of tailed viruses may be attached.

label: icosahedral viral capsid, collar
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines icosahedral viral capsid, collar as: A small disk located at the base of some icosahedral virus capsids.

label: icosahedral viral capsid, neck
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines icosahedral viral capsid, neck as: A region of constriction located below the head and above the tail sheath of viruses with contractile tails (Myoviridae).

label: viral capsid, decoration
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines viral capsid, decoration as: Component of the virus capsid (head), located on the outer head surface. Involved in the stabilization of the head structure and usually non-essential.

label: viral membrane
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines viral membrane as: The lipid bilayer of a virion, a complete fully infectious extracellular virus particle.

label: bacterial-type flagellum filament
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines bacterial-type flagellum filament as: The long (approximately 20 nm), thin external structure of the bacterial-type flagellum, which acts as a propeller.

label: A band
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines A band as: The dark-staining region of a sarcomere, in which myosin thick filaments are present; the center is traversed by the paler H zone, which in turn contains the M line.

label: actin filament branch point
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines actin filament branch point as: The part of an actin filament where the structure forks.

label: apoplast
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines apoplast as: The cell membranes and intracellular regions in a plant are connected through plasmodesmata, and plants may be described as having two major compartments: the living symplast and the non-living apoplast. The apoplast is external to the plasma membrane and includes cell walls, intercellular spaces and the lumen of dead structures such as xylem vessels. Water and solutes pass freely through it.

label: etioplast prolamellar body
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines etioplast prolamellar body as: A three dimensional regular lattice found in etioplasts. It is composed of a continuous system of tubules but when exposed to light the symmetrical arrangement is rapidly lost as tubules become pinched off into two dimensional sections of lattice. These for perforated sheets of membrane that move apart, extend and increase, finally establishing the typical granal and intergranal lamellae of the mature chloroplast.

label: postsynaptic endocytic zone
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines postsynaptic endocytic zone as: A stably positioned site of clathrin adjacent and physically attached to the postsynaptic specialization, which is the site of endocytosis of post-synaptic proteins.

label: cytosol
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines cytosol as: The part of the cytoplasm that does not contain organelles but which does contain other particulate matter, such as protein complexes.

label: intracellular immature spore
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines intracellular immature spore as: A cell or part of the cell that constitutes an early developmental stage of a spore, a small reproductive body that is highly resistant to desiccation and heat and is capable of growing into a new organism, produced especially by certain bacteria, fungi, algae, and nonflowering plants.

label: lysosomal glycocalyx
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines lysosomal glycocalyx as: The polysaccharide-based coating on the inner side of a lysosomal membrane. It may be involved in protecting the membrane from digestion by lysosomal enzymes.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, MS ring
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines bacterial-type flagellum basal body, MS ring as: One of the rings of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body; a double-flanged ring that anchors the basal body to the cytoplasmic membrane.

label: distal axon
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines distal axon as: That part of an axon close to and including the growth cone or the axon terminus.

label: ciliary cap
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines ciliary cap as: An intracellular compartmentalized cilium structure found in insect spermatids which is bounded by a membrane derived from the invagination of the cell membrane that remains associated with the primary cilium as it is internalized. The ciliary cap is maintained at the end of the axoneme distal to the centriole and is separated from the cytosolic axoneme/cytoplasm by a putative transition zone, which may extend into the ciliary cap, and include a structure at the base of the ciliary cap termed the ring centriole.

label: dense nuclear body
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines dense nuclear body as: A location in the host cell nucleus where viral proteins colocalize late in infection prior to the onset of viral DNA synthesis. More than one site can be present simultaneously.

label: M band
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines M band as: The midline of aligned thick filaments in a sarcomere; location of specific proteins that link thick filaments. Depending on muscle type the M band consists of different numbers of M lines.

label: photoreceptor inner segment
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines photoreceptor inner segment as: The inner segment of a vertebrate photoreceptor containing mitochondria, ribosomes and membranes where opsin molecules are assembled and passed to be part of the outer segment discs.

label: surface coat of collagen and cuticulin-based cuticle extracellular matrix
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines surface coat of collagen and cuticulin-based cuticle extracellular matrix as: An electron dense, amorphous envelope that comprises the outermost layer of the cuticle. The surface coat is loosely apposed to the epicuticle, has distinct biochemical properties, is synthesized by cells other than the underlying hypodermis, and is labile. In addition to serving as a lubricant to protect against abrasion and dehydration, the surface coat may also play important roles in infection and immune evasion. An example of this component is found in Caenorhabditis elegans.

label: bacterial-type flagellum secretion apparatus
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines bacterial-type flagellum secretion apparatus as: A part of the bacterial-type flagellum that is located at the cytoplasmic side of the MS ring and composed of six membrane proteins (FlhA, FlhB, FliP, FliQ, FliR, and FliO, or orthologs thereof) and three soluble proteins (FliI, FliH, and FliJ, or orthologs thereof) in the cytoplasm. It is responsible for secretion of flagellar type III protein substrates, including the proteins of the flagellar rod, hook, and filament.

label: neuron projection branch point
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines neuron projection branch point as: The location where a secondary projection arises from a neuron projection.

label: photoreceptor outer segment
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines photoreceptor outer segment as: The outer segment of a vertebrate photoreceptor that contains a stack of membrane discs embedded with photoreceptor proteins.

label: germ tube
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines germ tube as: The slender tubular outgrowth first produced by most spores in germination.

label: mating projection base
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines mating projection base as: The region where the mating projection meets the bulk of the cell, in unicellular fungi exposed to mating pheromone.

label: lateral plasma membrane
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines lateral plasma membrane as: The portion of the plasma membrane at the lateral side of the cell. In epithelial cells, lateral plasma membranes are on the sides of cells which lie at the interface of adjacent cells.

label: nexine
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines nexine as: The inner, non-sculptured part of the exine which lies below the sexine.

label: mitochondrial membrane scission site
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines mitochondrial membrane scission site as: The site on the mitochondrial membrane where the separation of a single continuous mitochondrial membrane into two membranes occurs as a final step in mitochondrial fission.

label: ventral disc crossbridge
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines ventral disc crossbridge as: Structure horizontally linking adjacent microribbons of the ventral disc in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). The composition of crossbridges is not fully known yet.

label: extracellular region
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines extracellular region as: The space external to the outermost structure of a cell. For cells without external protective or external encapsulating structures this refers to space outside of the plasma membrane. This term covers the host cell environment outside an intracellular parasite.

label: cortical dynamic polarity patch
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines cortical dynamic polarity patch as: A region of the cell cortex that contains a higher concentration of growth polarity factors than the surrounding cortex and that changes position over time. An example is found in fission yeast cells during early mating, in which the GTPase Cdc42 dynamically to discrete zones within the cortex prior to shmoo formation.

label: cell trailing edge membrane
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines cell trailing edge membrane as: The portion of the plasma membrane surrounding the trailing edge of a motile cell.

label: granular component
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines granular component as: A structure found in the nucleolus, which contains nearly completed preribosomal particles destined for the cytoplasm.

label: distal portion of axoneme
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines distal portion of axoneme as: The portion of the axoneme that is close to the tip of the cilium.

label: mitochondrial crista
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines mitochondrial crista as: Any of the inward folds of the mitochondrial inner membrane. Their number, extent, and shape differ in mitochondria from different tissues and organisms. They appear to be devices for increasing the surface area of the mitochondrial inner membrane, where the enzymes of electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation are found. Their shape can vary with the respiratory state of the mitochondria.

label: dinoflagellate apex
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines dinoflagellate apex as: The anterior most point of a dinoflagellate epicone.

label: extrahaustorial matrix
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines extrahaustorial matrix as: The space between the symbiont plasma membrane and the extrahaustorial membrane of the host.

label: nuclear envelope adjacent to nuclear pore complex
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines nuclear envelope adjacent to nuclear pore complex as: The region of the nuclear envelope situated in close proximity to a nuclear pore complex.

label: preprophase band
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines preprophase band as: A dense band of microtubules, 1-3 pm wide, that appears just beneath the cell membrane before the start of cell division in the cells of higher plants. It precedes the onset of prophase and then disappears as mitosis begins, yet it somehow determines the plane of orientation of the new cell plate forming in late telophase and marks the zone of the parental cell wall where fusion with the growing cell plate ultimately occurs.

label: left lateral basal body pair
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines left lateral basal body pair as: Set of two basal bodies found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). It comprises the anterior and ventral basal bodies located to the right of the left nucleus of the trophozoite when viewed dorsally.

label: C zone
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines C zone as: A region of the A band in which myosin-binding protein C is located and that can be seen by electron microscopy. This is a functional zone that also includes myosin.

label: ascus epiplasm
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines ascus epiplasm as: Ascus cytoplasm that is not packaged into ascospores.

label: mitochondrial inner boundary membrane
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines mitochondrial inner boundary membrane as: The portion of the mitochondrial inner membrane that is not invaginated to form cristae. The inner boundary membrane lies parallel to the outer membrane.

label: spindle matrix
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines spindle matrix as: A proteinaceous, nuclear-derived structure that embeds the microtubule spindle apparatus from pole to pole in a microtubule-independent manner during mitosis.

label: prospore membrane spindle pole body attachment site
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines prospore membrane spindle pole body attachment site as: The region of the prospore membrane to which the spindle pole body (SPB) is anchored; the prospore membrane extends from the SPB attachment site to surround the spore nucleus.

label: cytosolic region
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines cytosolic region as: Any (proper) part of the cytosol of a single cell of sufficient size to still be considered cytosol.

label: epicuticle of collagen and cuticulin-based cuticle extracellular matrix
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines epicuticle of collagen and cuticulin-based cuticle extracellular matrix as: A lipid-containing layer of cuticle that lies between the cortical layer and the surface coat. An example of this component is found in Caenorhabditis elegans.

label: immunological synapse
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines immunological synapse as: An area of close contact between a lymphocyte (T-, B-, or natural killer cell) and a target cell formed through the clustering of particular signaling and adhesion molecules and their associated membrane rafts on both the lymphocyte and the target cell and facilitating activation of the lymphocyte, transfer of membrane from the target cell to the lymphocyte, and in some situations killing of the target cell through release of secretory granules and/or death-pathway ligand-receptor interaction.

label: nuclear lamina
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines nuclear lamina as: The fibrous, electron-dense layer lying on the nucleoplasmic side of the inner membrane of a cell nucleus, composed of lamin filaments. The polypeptides of the lamina are thought to be concerned in the dissolution of the nuclear envelope and its re-formation during mitosis. The lamina is composed of lamin A and lamin C filaments cross-linked into an orthogonal lattice, which is attached via lamin B to the inner nuclear membrane through interactions with a lamin B receptor, an IFAP, in the membrane.

label: endexine
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines endexine as: The inner part of the exine, which stains.

label: kinetoplast
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines kinetoplast as: A sub-structure within the large single mitochondrion of kinetoplastid parasites and which is closely associated with the flagellar pocket and basal body of the flagellum.

label: medial membrane band
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines medial membrane band as: A sterol-rich region of the plasma membrane which forms at the cell surface overlying the contractile ring and spreads into the invaginating plasma membrane surrounding the septum.

label: ventral disc supernumerary microtubule array
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines ventral disc supernumerary microtubule array as: A partial left-handed spiral array of microtubules that lies generally dorsal to the main ventral disc microtubule array in Giardia species (trophozoite stage).

label: T-tubule
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines T-tubule as: Invagination of the plasma membrane of a muscle cell that extends inward from the cell surface around each myofibril. The ends of T-tubules make contact with the sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane.

label: myelin sheath adaxonal region
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines myelin sheath adaxonal region as: The region of the myelin sheath nearest to the axon.

label: spermatid residual body
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines spermatid residual body as: A membrane-bounded, anucleate mass of cytoplasm that is separated from one or more developing male germ cells during spermatogenesis and discarded. The residual body receives most of the cytoplasm and organelles not required by the spermatid or spermatozoon, such as ribosomes, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi, and excess cytoskeletal components, and is subsequently degraded, typically by phagocytosis by somatic cells of the gonad (e.g. Sertoli cells in vertebrates, gonadal sheath cells in nematodes) or by extrusion into the reproductive tract.

label: leading edge membrane
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines leading edge membrane as: The portion of the plasma membrane surrounding the leading edge of a motile cell.

label: mitotic nuclear bridge midzone membrane domain
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines mitotic nuclear bridge midzone membrane domain as: A nuclear membrane part at the midzone of the mitotic nuclear bridge. The midzone forms a bulge that is enriched in nuclear pores that lack baskets.

label: dense fibrillar component
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines dense fibrillar component as: A structure found in the nucleolus, which contains newly synthesized preribosomal RNA (pre-rRNA) and a collection of proteins.

label: bacterial-type flagellum hook-filament junction
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines bacterial-type flagellum hook-filament junction as: The region of the bacterial-type flagellum where the hook and filament meet.

label: inner dense plaque of desmosome
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines inner dense plaque of desmosome as: The desmosomal part containing the C-termini of desmoplakins which interact with the keratin intermediate filaments, serving to tether the intermediate filaments to the plasma membrane.

label: I band
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines I band as: A region of a sarcomere that appears as a light band on each side of the Z disc, comprising a region of the sarcomere where thin (actin) filaments are not overlapped by thick (myosin) filaments; contains actin, troponin, and tropomyosin; each sarcomere includes half of an I band at each end.

label: virus-like capsid
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines virus-like capsid as: A protein coat that surrounds nucleic acid to form a structure similar to a virus capsid. Virus-like capsids are non-infectious and are encoded by endogenous (non-viral) genes. Fly and tetrapod Arc (ancestrally-related to retrotransposon Gag) are examples of proteins that can self-assemble into capsid-like structures which encapsulate Arc mRNA and mediate the intercellular transmission of RNA.

label: endomembrane system
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines endomembrane system as: A collection of membranous structures involved in transport within the cell. The main components of the endomembrane system are endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi bodies, vesicles, cell membrane and nuclear envelope. Members of the endomembrane system pass materials through each other or though the use of vesicles.

label: organelle
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines organelle as: Organized structure of distinctive morphology and function. Includes the nucleus, mitochondria, plastids, vacuoles, vesicles, ribosomes and the cytoskeleton, and prokaryotic structures such as anammoxosomes and pirellulosomes. Excludes the plasma membrane.

label: axon hillock
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines axon hillock as: Portion of the neuronal cell soma from which the axon originates.

label: longitudinal sarcoplasmic reticulum
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines longitudinal sarcoplasmic reticulum as: The portion of the free sarcoplasmic reticulum consisting of longitudinal tubules that connect terminal cisternae.

label: DNA replication termination region
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines DNA replication termination region as: A chromosomal region that contains fork pausing elements influencing the progression and merging of DNA replication forks.

label: cell projection
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines cell projection as: A prolongation or process extending from a cell, e.g. a flagellum or axon.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, C ring
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines bacterial-type flagellum basal body, C ring as: Cytoplasmic ring located at the base of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body; acts as a rotor; includes three switch proteins, which generate torque and can change their conformational state in a bimodal fashion, so that the motor direction can switch between clockwise and counterclockwise.

label: mitotic actomyosin contractile ring, proximal layer
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines mitotic actomyosin contractile ring, proximal layer as: The region of the mitotic actomyosin ring adjacent to the plasma membrane where membrane bound scaffolds are located.

label: dityrosine layer of spore wall
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines dityrosine layer of spore wall as: The outermost layer of the spore wall, as described in Saccharomyces.

label: fibrillar center
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines fibrillar center as: A structure found most metazoan nucleoli, but not usually found in lower eukaryotes; surrounded by the dense fibrillar component; the zone of transcription from multiple copies of the pre-rRNA genes is in the border region between these two structures.

label: lysosomal matrix
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines lysosomal matrix as: A matrix composed of supramolecular assemblies of lysosomal enzymes and lipids which forms at a pH of 5.0 within the lysosome.

label: ventral disc microtubule array
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines ventral disc microtubule array as: A part of the ventral disc of Giardia species (trophozoite stage) consisting of a spiral array of microtubules linked to the ventral membrane. These microtubules form the base of the ventral disc dorsal microribbons that extend nearly perpendicular from the membrane.

label: foot layer
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines foot layer as: The inner layer of the ectexine.

label: reservosome membrane
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines reservosome membrane as: The lipid bilayer surrounding a reservosome.

label: central region of growth cone
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines central region of growth cone as: The center of the migrating motile tip of a growing nerve cell axon or dendrite.

label: smooth endoplasmic reticulum cisterna
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines smooth endoplasmic reticulum cisterna as: A subcompartment of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum consisting of lumenal expansion into a flattened, disc-shaped cavity.

label: sperm head-tail coupling apparatus
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines sperm head-tail coupling apparatus as: A centrosome-based structure consisting of two cylindrical microtubule-based centrioles and associated components which anchors the flagellum to the sperm head.

label: ventral surface of cell
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines ventral surface of cell as: The surface of a migrating cell that is in contact with the substratum or cell layer.

label: satellite fibril
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines satellite fibril as: An axoneme part that is found in the flagella of mammalian sperm and is located in the middle piece between the outer dense fibers (on the concave side of outer dense fibers as seen in cross-section).

label: bacterial-type flagellum filament cap
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines bacterial-type flagellum filament cap as: The proteinaceous structure at the distal tip of the bacterial-type flagellar filament.

label: H zone
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines H zone as: A relatively pale zone traversing the center of the A band of a sarcomere, visible in relaxed muscle fibers; consists of the central portion of thick (myosin) filaments that are not overlapped by thin (actin) filaments.

label: basal labyrinth
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines basal labyrinth as: A region in the lower half of some cells formed from extensive infoldings of the basal plasma membrane; includes cytoplasm adjacent to the infolded membrane.

label: granum
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines granum as: Distinct stack of lamellae seen within chloroplasts. Grana contain the pigments, electron transfer compounds, and enzymes essential to the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.

label: perikaryon
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines perikaryon as: The portion of the cell soma (neuronal cell body) that excludes the nucleus.

label: phagocytic cup
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines phagocytic cup as: An invagination of the cell membrane formed by an actin dependent process during phagocytosis. Following internalization it is converted into a phagosome.

label: organelle membrane contact site
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines organelle membrane contact site as: A zone of apposition between the membranes of an organelle with another membrane, either another membrane of the same organelle, a membrane of another organelle, or the plasma membrane. Membrane contact sites (MCSs) are structured by bridging complexes. They are specialized for communication, including the efficient traffic of small molecules such as Ca2+ ions and lipids, as well as enzyme-substrate interactions.

label: ring centriole
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines ring centriole as: A ring-like structure observed at the base of the ciliary cap of insect spermatids. This structure may anchor the axoneme to the ciliary cap membrane and/or act as a diffusion barrier, proposed to be analogous to the annulus of mammalian sperm flagellum.

label: site of polarized growth
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines site of polarized growth as: Any part of a cell where non-isotropic growth takes place.

label: synaptic cleft
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines synaptic cleft as: The narrow gap that separates the presynaptic and postsynaptic membranes, into which neurotransmitter is released.

label: perinuclear region of cytoplasm
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines perinuclear region of cytoplasm as: Cytoplasm situated near, or occurring around, the nucleus.

label: synaptonemal structure
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines synaptonemal structure as: A proteinaceous scaffold found between homologous chromosomes during meiosis.

label: actomyosin
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines actomyosin as: Any complex of actin, myosin, and accessory proteins.

label: nucleoplasm
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines nucleoplasm as: That part of the nuclear content other than the chromosomes or the nucleolus.

label: mucus layer
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines mucus layer as: An extracellular region part that consists of a protective layer of mucus secreted by epithelial cells lining tubular organs of the body such as the colon or secreted into fluids such as saliva. Mucus is a viscous slimy secretion consisting of mucins (i.e. highly glycosylated mucin proteins) and various inorganic salts dissolved in water, with suspended epithelial cells and leukocytes.

label: chitosan layer of spore wall
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines chitosan layer of spore wall as: The second outermost layer of the spore wall, as described in Saccharomyces.

label: ventral disc dorsal microribbon
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines ventral disc dorsal microribbon as: Trilaminar structure extending perpendicularly into the cytoplasm along the length of ventral disc microtubules in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). Constituents of dorsal microribbons (also called dorsal ribbons or microribbons) include alpha-coiled-helix proteins approximately 29 to 38 kDa in size. These proteins line the edges of the microribbons but are not found in microtubules. Tubulins are not found in microribbons.

label: reservosome matrix
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines reservosome matrix as: A matrix composed of planar membranes, vesicles and lipid inclusions within the reservosome.

label: peripheral region of growth cone
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines peripheral region of growth cone as: The non-central region or periphery of the migrating motile tip of a growing nerve cell axon or dendrite.

label: centrosomal core
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines centrosomal core as: The core region of the centrosome, a layered structure containing proteins, surrounded by the centrosomal corona. The core duplicates once per cell cycle at the G2/M transition when two outer layers form the mitotic spindle poles.

label: cell division site
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines cell division site as: The eventual plane of cell division (also known as cell cleavage or cytokinesis) in a dividing cell. In Eukaryotes, the cleavage apparatus, composed of septin structures and the actomyosin contractile ring, forms along this plane, and the mitotic, or meiotic, spindle is aligned perpendicular to the division plane. In bacteria, the cell division site is generally located at mid-cell and is the site at which the cytoskeletal structure, the Z-ring, assembles.

label: extracellular core region of desmosome
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines extracellular core region of desmosome as: The desmosomal part containing the desmosomal cadherins, desmogleins and desmocollins, that establish contact and adhere to neighboring cells in a Ca2+-dependent manner.

label: unicellular trichome branch
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines unicellular trichome branch as: A cell projection part that is a branch of a unicellular trichome.

label: mitotic nuclear bridge stalk
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines mitotic nuclear bridge stalk as: Either of the regions of a mitotic nuclear bridge proximal to the main portion of each daughter nucleus. The nuclear envelope in the stalk regions is depleted of nuclear pore complexes.

label: cone matrix sheath
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines cone matrix sheath as: A biochemically and structurally distinct domain of the retinal interphotoreceptor matrix that is specifically associated with cone photoreceptor cell inner and outer segments.

label: bacterial-type flagellum hook
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines bacterial-type flagellum hook as: The portion of the bacterial-type flagellum that connects the filament to the basal body.

label: actin body
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines actin body as: An amorphous cytoskeletal structure consisting of aggregated actin filaments and associated proteins (including fibrin and capping protein) in which there is little or no actin filament turnover. In yeast (S. pombe and S. cerevisiae) these are found only in quiescent cells and are thought to serve as a reserve store of actin.

label: sarcomere
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines sarcomere as: The repeating unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z discs.

label: starch grain
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines starch grain as: Plant storage body for amylose and amylopectin, 1-100um in diameter. Also contains small amounts of enzymes, amino acids, lipids and nucleic acids. The shape of the grain varies widely amongst species, but is often spherical or disk-shaped.

label: nucleoplasmic periphery of the nuclear pore complex
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines nucleoplasmic periphery of the nuclear pore complex as: Nucleoplasm situated in close proximity and peripheral to a nuclear pore complex.

label: cluster of actin-based cell projections
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines cluster of actin-based cell projections as: A cell part consisting of multiple, closely packed actin-based cell projections.

label: sperm fibrous sheath
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines sperm fibrous sheath as: A cytoskeletal structure surrounding the axoneme and outer dense fibers of the sperm flagellum. Consists of two longitudinal columns connected by closely arrayed semicircular ribs that assemble from distal to proximal throughout spermiogenesis. The fibrous sheath probably influences the degree of flexibility, plane of flagellar motion, and the shape of the flagellar beat.

label: Schmidt-Lanterman incisure
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines Schmidt-Lanterman incisure as: Regions within compact myelin in which the cytoplasmic faces of the enveloping myelin sheath are not tightly juxtaposed, and include cytoplasm from the cell responsible for making the myelin. Schmidt-Lanterman incisures occur in the compact myelin internode, while lateral loops are analogous structures found in the paranodal region adjacent to the nodes of Ranvier.

label: subpellicular network
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines subpellicular network as: A mechanically stable cytoskeletal structure associated with the cytoplasmic face of the pellicle and surrounding the microtubule-based cytoskeleton.

label: dinoflagellate hypocone
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines dinoflagellate hypocone as: The part of a dinoflagellate cell below the cingulum; also referred to as the posterior portion of a dinoflagellate cell. It is separated from the epicone by the cingulum.

label: chromatin
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines chromatin as: The ordered and organized complex of DNA, protein, and sometimes RNA, that forms the chromosome.

label: intercellular bridge
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines intercellular bridge as: A direct connection between the cytoplasm of two cells that is formed following the completion of cleavage furrow ingression during cell division. They are usually present only briefly prior to completion of cytokinesis. However, in some cases, such as the bridges between germ cells during their development, they become stabilised.

label: ciliary pocket collar
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines ciliary pocket collar as: A constriction site at the junction of the plasma, flagellar and flagellar pocket membranes where the flagellum emerges from the cell body. Observed in some unicellular eukaryotic species such as Chlamydomonas, Giardia and Trypanosoma.

label: axonemal central bridge
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines axonemal central bridge as: Part of the 9+2 axoneme, that occurs in most motile cilia, consisting of the two bridges which connect the central pair of single microtubules.

label: annular furrow extracellular matrix
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines annular furrow extracellular matrix as: The extracellular matrix part that is a regularly spaced indentation in the outer cortical layer of the cuticle. The pattern of annular furrows corresponds to sites of invaginations in hypodermal cell membranes that, in turn, correspond to submembranous regions where actin microfilament bundles assemble early in lethargus, the first phase of the molting cycle in which activity and feeding decline.

label: half bridge of spindle pole body
summary: The Gene Ontology (via EMBL-EBI QuickGO) defines half bridge of spindle pole body as: Structure adjacent to the plaques of the spindle pole body.
